fields.name: 2026 Amiga Corporation–Hyperion settlement

fields.what: Signed on 5 June 2026 and announced on 4 August, the settlement ends all litigation and replaces the 2009 agreement. fields.what: An officially licensed Amiga version of Blue Byte's 1996 city-building strategy game, released on 18 October 2025 at Amiga40 in Mönchengladbach after a gamescom 2025 preview. It needs an AGA Amiga with a 68040 at 40 MHz and 32 MB fast RAM, with PowerPC builds for AmigaOS 4.1 and AmigaOS 3.2 with WarpUP. Digital, boxed and a sold-out 100-copy wooden Collector's Edition were offered; updates in May 2026 improved the 68k, PPC and OS4 versions.
fields.why: A game that famously skipped the Amiga in 1996 finally shipped for it, with the rights holder's licence. It is the clearest example of a modern commercial Amiga release backed by a major publisher, and a flagship of the Amiga40 event.

fields.name: Evercade Amiga cartridges
fields.by: Blaze Entertainment with Team17, The Bitmap Brothers and other publishers
fields.what: A line of licensed Evercade cartridges, packaged in blue home-computer cases, running Amiga games through emulation on Blaze's handheld and TV systems with save states and PAL 50 Hz. Team17 Collection 1 (May 2023) was the first, with ten Team17 titles; The Bitmap Brothers Collection 2 (September 2024, cartridge C08) added Cadaver, Cadaver: The Payoff, Gods, Magic Pockets, The Chaos Engine 2 and the PlayStation Z.
fields.why: The first legal Amiga emulation on a handheld format, announced at Amiga37 in October 2022 and part of the licensing network that now includes Retro Games Ltd and Blaze in the 2026 settlement. It sits next to the THEA mini-computers as another consumer route to licensed Amiga games.

fields.name: Kickstart Amiga Expo
fields.by: Kickstart Amiga Group (founded by Ravi Abbott of The Retro Hour)
fields.what: The UK's biggest Amiga show, a combined trade show, user-group meeting and talks programme. Kickstart 01 ran in July 2023 at Meadow Lane, Nottingham; Kickstart 02 on 29-30 June 2024 had about 800 attendees expected; a 40th-anniversary Kickstart followed in September 2025; and Kickstart Expo 3.0 moved to The Reach Conference Centre in Derby on 7-8 August 2026, where Amiga Corporation outlined its AmigaOS 3 plans. Attendees receive free Amiga Forever and C64 Forever licences.
